pages.lesson:
LESSON: CAPACITY

Grade: PP2
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.4: Capacity

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Capacity. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: how many small ones b) compare sizes of containers big and small containers by can be filled?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate the use of objects comparing big and small of different sizes in the containers by telling

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Today’s maths focus is Capacity.

• Start with objects you can touch or draw — stones, sticks, bottle tops, or drawings in your book.

• Say the steps aloud as you work so you do not skip a stage.

• Check your answer with a second method or by estimating.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market, count 10 mangoes and put them in 2 groups of 5.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row and write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and receive 5 more, you have 12 shillings.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Solve three short problems about Capacity using drawings.
2. Explain one solution to a partner in your own words.
3. Make up one new word problem set in your county or school.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five practice questions and solve them in your book.
2. Show your working clearly — not only the final answer.
3. Teach a younger learner one idea from this lesson with bottle tops or drawings.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. In groups or pairs, individually, learners tell how much a container can hold compared to another one of a different size
2. Watch a video on filling and emptying containers.
3. Food and nutrition: filling containers using different types of seeds and food staffs;
4. Environmental activities as they play filling and emptying

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how many small ones b) compare sizes of containers big and small containers by can be filled?
2. Which container holds emptying using different the big ones and vice versa more/less?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Use objects or drawings when a sum feels hard.
2. Check every answer.
3. Capacity is used in real Kenyan life — market, school, and home.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
